mainTopic: חליצה or ייבום with a יבמה who turns out to be pregnant, and whether such acts count
overview: This amud deals with a surprise: a יבם does חליצה or ייבום, and then it turns out the widow was pregnant from her late husband. The משנה rules that everything depends on whether the baby is viable. A viable baby means there was never a יבום bond, so the חליצה is void and the ייבום was a forbidden marriage. A non-viable baby means the bond was real, so the חליצה counts and the ייבום stands. The גמרא then brings a dispute about a חליצה done with a pregnant woman who later miscarried. רבי יוחנן says it counts, and ריש לקיש says it does not. Each side tests its view against the משנה's wording, in two versions of the exchange. A ברייתא about the widow's צרה leads אביי to say that everyone agrees ביאה with a pregnant woman does not count, and that the argument is only about חליצה. רבא challenges that split at the end of the amud, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חליצה, then a viable baby is born
steps.stepSummary: If a man did חליצה and the widow then gives birth to a viable child, the חליצה was meaningless. No family prohibitions are created, and she may still marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man does חליצה with his brother's widow, and it turns out she was pregnant and she gives birth to a viable child, he stays permitted to her relatives, she stays permitted to his relatives, and she is not disqualified from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first case: חליצה was done, and then a healthy, viable baby is born. It rules that the חליצה counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה only applies when the dead brother left no children. A viable baby shows he did leave a child, so there was never a זיקה (levirate bond) and the חליצה was an empty act. That means none of the usual results of חליצה apply: no ban on each other's relatives, and no status of חלוצה that would bar her from a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: One who performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases a יבמה
His יבמה, his dead brother's childless widow
Pregnant
A viable child, one able to survive
Her female relatives / his male relatives
The priesthood, meaning marriage to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Normally a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן, just like a divorcée. That rule does not apply here, because a viable child shows this was never a real חליצה at all.

phrases.english: One who performs chalitza with his yevama
and she is found to be pregnant and gives birth,
when the child is viable —
he is permitted to her relatives,
and she is permitted to his relatives,
and he did not disqualify her from the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חליצה, if a viable child is born, the חליצה is void: no prohibition on relatives and no disqualification from כהונה.

steps.title: חליצה, then a non-viable baby is born
steps.stepSummary: If the baby is not viable, the חליצה was real. They become forbidden to each other's relatives, and she is disqualified from marrying a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the child is not viable, he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and the חליצה disqualifies her from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the flip side of the same חליצה case: now the baby is not viable. The משנה rules that the חליצה was fully valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-viable baby does not count as a surviving child, so the dead brother really did die childless. The יבום bond was real, and the חליצה actually did something. All of its normal results apply, as if they had been married and divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden (masculine / feminine)
He disqualified her

phrases.english: if the child is not viable —
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives,
and he has disqualified her from the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite outcome of the same חליצה case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חליצה, if the child is not viable, the חליצה is valid, with all its usual prohibitions, including disqualification from כהונה.
steps.whatToRemember: For חליצה: a viable baby means the חליצה never counted. A non-viable baby means it counted fully.

steps.title: ייבום, then a viable baby is born
steps.stepSummary: If the brother married the widow through ייבום and then a viable child is born, the marriage was really forbidden as אשת אח. He must divorce her, and both must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man marries his יבמה, and it turns out she was pregnant and she gives birth to a viable child, he must send her away, and they are obligated to bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the second case: instead of חליצה, the brother did ייבום. Then a viable baby is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A viable child means there was never a מצוה of יבום. His dead brother's wife was simply forbidden to him as אשת אח, an איסור כרת. Since they sinned by mistake, they must separate, and each brings a קרבן חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries, here meaning performs ייבום
He must send her out, meaning divorce her
They are obligated to bring an offering, a חטאת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ייבום is only permitted because of the מצוה. Without the מצוה, the full איסור of אשת אח comes back.

phrases.english: One who consummates levirate marriage with his yevama
and she is found to be pregnant and gives birth,
when the child is viable —
he must send her out, and they are obligated to bring an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹנֵס אֶת יְבִמְתּוֹ וְנִמְצֵאת מְעוּבֶּרֶת וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same viable/non-viable test to ייבום instead of חליצה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After ייבום, if a viable child is born, the marriage was forbidden. He must divorce her, and both bring a קרבן.

steps.title: ייבום, then a non-viable baby is born
steps.stepSummary: If the baby is not viable, the ייבום was a valid מצוה, and he may stay married to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the child is not viable, he may keep her as his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the flip side of the ייבום case: the baby is not viable. The משנה rules that the marriage stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-viable baby does not count as a child, so the dead brother died childless and the מצוה of יבום really applied. The ייבום was proper, so there is no sin and no need to separate.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her, meaning stay married to her

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה turns on one question: is the baby viable? Viable means there was no יבום bond, so חליצה is void and ייבום is forbidden. Not viable means the bond was real, so חליצה is valid and ייבום stands.

phrases.english: And if the child is not viable —
he may maintain her as his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite outcome of the same ייבום case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After ייבום, if the child is not viable, the ייבום is valid and he keeps her.

steps.title: A baby of uncertain father after ייבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a case where the baby might belong to the dead husband or to the יבם. He must divorce her, the child is כשר, and both bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is unclear whether the baby is a nine-month baby from the first husband or a seven-month baby from the יבם, he must send her away. The child is כשר, and both must bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case: after ייבום the baby is born, and we cannot tell whose baby it is. It rules on what happens to the couple and to the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is the dead husband's, then the ייבום was really a forbidden marriage to a brother's wife, as in Step 3. If the baby is the יבם's own, then the ייבום was a valid מצוה, as in Step 4. Because of the doubt he must divorce her, and they bring an אשם תלוי, the offering for a possible sin. The child is kosher either way, because it was not conceived through a forbidden relationship in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; we cannot tell which way it is.
A baby born after nine months of pregnancy.
A baby born after only seven months of pregnancy.
He must send her out, meaning he must divorce her.
A 'hanging' guilt-offering, brought when someone is unsure whether they sinned.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the child is a ממזר because the marriage might have been forbidden. The child was conceived either by the first husband while he was married to her, or by the יבם after a valid ייבום. Neither one is a forbidden relationship, so the child is כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: When it is unclear whose baby it is, he must divorce her, the child is כשר, and both bring an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether it is a nine-month baby of the first husband,
phrases.notes: The case: she gave birth seven months after the ייבום, so either timing is possible.

phrases.english: or a seven-month baby of the latter one,
he must send her out, and the child is kosher.
And they are obligated in an אשם תלוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן, סָפֵק בֶּן שִׁבְעָה לָאַחֲרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a doubtful case that falls between the two clear cases in Steps 3 and 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is uncertain whose child it is, he must divorce her, the child is כשר, and both bring an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Dispute: חליצה with a pregnant woman who then miscarried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a dispute. רבי יוחנן says she does not need another חליצה, and ריש לקיש says she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone does חליצה with a pregnant widow and she then miscarries, רבי יוחנן says she does not need חליצה from the brothers. ריש לקיש says she does need חליצה from the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a dispute between two אמוראים about a חליצה that was done while the widow was pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the baby did not survive, she really was tied to the brothers and needed ייבום or חליצה. The only question is whether the חליצה done back when she was pregnant counts. רבי יוחנן says it counts, and ריש לקיש says they must do it again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated': this opens a dispute between אמוראים.
A pregnant woman.
She miscarried.
A חליצה from one of the dead man's brothers, which frees her to marry others.

steps.confusionAlert: The two do not argue about whether she was tied to the brothers. Since she miscarried, she definitely was. They argue only about whether the earlier חליצה, done while she was pregnant, worked.

phrases.english: גמרא: It was stated:
One who does חליצה with a pregnant woman, and she miscarried:
רבי יוחנן said:
She does not need חליצה from the brothers.
ריש לקיש said:
She needs חליצה from the brothers.
phrases.notes: He means she needs a new חליצה, because the first one did not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a new dispute connected to the משנה's cases of a pregnant widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no new חליצה is needed. ריש לקיש: a new חליצה is needed.

steps.title: The reason behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that חליצה and ביאה with a pregnant woman count. ריש לקיש holds that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says no new חליצה is needed, because חליצה with a pregnant woman counts as חליצה, and ביאה with a pregnant woman counts as ביאה. ריש לקיש says a new חליצה is needed, because neither one counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion and adds the principle behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute now becomes a general rule, not just a ruling about חליצה. Each side applies its view to both חליצה and ביאה. According to רבי יוחנן, a ייבום done while she was pregnant would also make them married. According to ריש לקיש, it would not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is called a חליצה, meaning it counts as a real חליצה.
Marital relations; here, the act that makes ייבום happen.
It is not called that, meaning it does not count.

steps.whyThisMatters: The way each side treats ביאה matches the way it treats חליצה. This shows they hold one shared principle about acts done with a pregnant יבמה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֲלִיצָה מִן הָאַחִין,
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said she does not need חליצה from the brothers, because:
the חליצה of a pregnant woman is called a חליצה,
and ביאה with a pregnant woman is called a ביאה.

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: צְרִיכָה חֲלִיצָה מִן הָאַחִין,
phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said she needs חליצה from the brothers, because:
the חליצה of a pregnant woman is not called a חליצה,
and ביאה with a pregnant woman is not called a ביאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two rulings in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: חליצה and ביאה with a pregnant woman count. ריש לקיש: they do not count.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the dispute depends on, and answers that it could be either a פסוק or a סברא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they argue about? If you want, say it is about a פסוק. If you want, say it is about a סברא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the disagreement. It names two possible directions: a פסוק or plain reasoning. This sets up the next move, where each direction will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we know what each side holds, but not why. This line announces that the גמרא will offer two separate explanations. One will be based on how a פסוק is read, and the other on logic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they argue?': a question asking for the root of a dispute.
'If you wish, say': it introduces one of two possible explanations.
A פסוק from the תורה.
Logical reasoning.

phrases.english: About what do they argue?
If you wish, say a פסוק,
and if you wish, say a סברא.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִפַּלְגִי? אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the principles stated in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying source or reasoning causes רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש to disagree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two directions are offered, a פסוק or a סברא. Each will be explained in the steps that follow.

steps.title: The reasoning approach: רבי יוחנן says the truth is revealed after the fact
steps.stepSummary: If the dispute is about a סברא, רבי יוחנן reasons that if we knew for sure she would miscarry, she would clearly be fit for חליצה and ייבום. So when she does miscarry, it is revealed after the fact that the act was always valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the argument is about logic. רבי יוחנן thinks like this: If אליהו came and told us this pregnant woman will miscarry, wouldn't she be fit for חליצה and ייבום right now? So now too, when she ends up miscarrying, it becomes clear after the fact that she was fit all along.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the first possible root of the dispute, a סברא, starting with רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן uses an imaginary test: if a נביא told us she will miscarry, nobody would doubt she needs חליצה or ייבום. The miscarriage that actually happens tells us the same thing, just later. So the act done while she was pregnant was valid from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say. Introduces one possible explanation.
Logical reasoning, as opposed to a source in a פסוק.
אליהו the prophet. Here he is a way of saying 'if we knew the future for certain.'
Miscarries.
The matter is revealed after the fact. What happens later shows what was true all along.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is a matter of logical reasoning:
Rabbi Yochanan holds:
If Eliyahu would come and say
that this woman who became pregnant will miscarry,

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָאו בַּת חֲלִיצָה וְיִבּוּם הִיא?
phrases.english: is she not fit for chalitza and yibum?
Now too,
the matter will be revealed retroactively.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the 'סברא' option named in step 8, starting with רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוחנן, the dispute rests on the idea that a later miscarriage reveals after the fact that the חליצה or ייבום was always valid.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rejects the idea of revealing after the fact
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש does not accept that a later miscarriage reveals after the fact that the act was valid. At the time of the act she was pregnant, so it did not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: We do not say that the matter is revealed after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's side of the סברא: he does not accept רבי יוחנן's 'revealed after the fact' reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, we judge the act by what we knew when it was done. At that moment there was a fetus that might be born alive, so the חליצה or ייבום did not count. A later miscarriage does not go back and fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the אמורא who argues with רבי יוחנן here.
We do not say. This rejects a line of reasoning.
Said.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
We do not say "the matter will be revealed retroactively."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the סברא from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A later miscarriage does not make a חליצה or ייבום done during pregnancy valid after the fact.

steps.title: The verse approach: two readings of 'and he has no child'
steps.stepSummary: If the dispute is about a פסוק, רבי יוחנן reads 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ' simply: this man has no child, so ייבום applies. ריש לקיש reads it as 'look into him carefully,' and a fetus counts as something to look into.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say the argument is about a פסוק. רבי יוחנן holds: the Torah said 'and he has no son,' and this man has none. ריש לקיש holds: 'and he has no son' means 'look carefully into him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second possible root of the dispute: a different reading of the פסוק about ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the words plainly: there is no child, so ייבום applies, and a fetus that ends in miscarriage was never a child. ריש לקיש reads אֵין (none) as עַיֵּין (examine). We must check carefully whether the dead man left offspring, and while she is pregnant there is a fetus, so the obligation hasn't started yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse in the תורה.
The Merciful One. A name for ה׳, used for what the תורה says.
'And he has no son.' The words in the פסוק of ייבום.
He does not have.
Look carefully into him. A דרש on the word אֵין.

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not changing the text of the פסוק. He is reading 'אֵין' as if it hinted at 'עַיֵּין' (examine), a sound-alike דרש.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is a matter of a verse:
Rabbi Yochanan holds:
"And he has no son," the Torah said,
and this man does not have one.
And Reish Lakish holds:
"And he has no son" means: look carefully into him.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: אֵין (none) sounds like עַיֵּין (look into). So check whether he left any offspring, and a fetus counts for now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second option from step 8 (a פסוק) in place of the סברא explained in steps 9 and 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue over 'וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ': simply 'he has no child' (רבי יוחנן) versus 'examine him first' (ריש לקיש).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the משנה's ruling on the priesthood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points to our משנה: if the baby is not viable, the חליצה creates relative-prohibitions and disqualifies her from כהונה. That fits his view that the חליצה counted. But why would she be disqualified according to ריש לקיש, who says it did not count?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: the משנה says if the baby is not viable, he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and she is disqualified from marrying a כהן. That works for me, since I say a חליצה with a pregnant woman counts, and that is why it disqualifies her. But according to you, who say it doesn't count, why is she disqualified from כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view using a ruling from our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real חליצה makes a woman forbidden to a כהן. The משנה says this חליצה, done while she was pregnant with a non-viable baby, does disqualify her. So it seems the חליצה counted, which goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him, using a source like a משנה or ברייתא.
Viable. A baby that will live.
Her female relatives.
Disqualified her from marrying a כהן.
It works well for. Sets up a 'this fits me, but not you' challenge.
חליצה done with a pregnant woman.

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the סוגיא from explaining both views to testing them against the משנה. ריש לקיש will need to explain the 'disqualified from כהונה' ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If the baby is not viable,
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives,
and it disqualified her from the priesthood.
It works well according to me,
since I say chalitza with a pregnant woman counts as chalitza;
that is why it disqualifies her.
But according to you,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרַתְּ חֲלִיצַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת לֹא שְׁמָהּ חֲלִיצָה,
phrases.english: since you say chalitza with a pregnant woman does not count as chalitza,
why does it disqualify her from the priesthood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both roots of the dispute are explained, רבי יוחנן tests ריש לקיש's view against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says this חליצה disqualifies her from כהונה, which only a real חליצה can do. So the חליצה must have counted.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers that the disqualification is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the משנה's ruling that she is disqualified from כהונה is only a rabbinic stringency, not a sign that the חליצה really counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: The disqualification is only rabbinic, just a stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question from step 12. He says the disqualification from כהונה is a rabbinic stringency, not Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן argued that if she is disqualified from כהונה, the חליצה must have counted. ריש לקיש answers that by Torah law the חליצה is nothing. The חכמים still disqualified her as an extra stringency, so the משנה does not prove that the חליצה worked.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not from the Torah
Merely as a stringency
He said to him (introduces an answer)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש answering רבי יוחנן's question from the last step.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law, and merely a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by saying the משנה's ruling is rabbinic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the ruling: the disqualification is rabbinic, not Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Disqualifying her from כהונה shows the חליצה counted by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חליצה counts for nothing by Torah law. The disqualification is only a rabbinic stringency.

steps.title: Second version: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, ריש לקיש uses the same משנה against רבי יוחנן. If the חליצה really counted, the משנה should have taught the bigger point: she does not need חליצה from the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן from the משנה: If the child is not viable, he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and she is disqualified from כהונה. This fits my view that the חליצה of a pregnant woman is not real חליצה. The משנה only says she is disqualified from כהונה as a stringency, and it does not say she is free from needing חליצה from the brothers. But according to you, the משנה should have said she does not need חליצה from the brothers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the argument, with the roles reversed. Now ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן using the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חליצה really counted, as רבי יוחנן says, then the biggest result is that she is fully free and needs no more חליצה. A משנה should teach that bigger point instead of the smaller one about כהונה. For ריש לקיש this is no problem, because in his view she does still need חליצה, and the כהונה ruling is only a stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces a second version)
He raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
Granted, according to my view (this fits)
A viable child, one who will live
A pregnant woman
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the very same משנה. In the first version רבי יוחנן uses it to attack ריש לקיש, and in this version ריש לקיש uses it to attack רבי יוחנן. Keep track of who is attacking whom.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If the child is not viable —
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives,
and he has disqualified her from the priesthood.
Granted, according to me,
since I say that the ḥalitza of a pregnant woman
is not considered ḥalitza,
that is why it teaches "he disqualified her from the priesthood"
as a stringency,
and it does not teach
"she does not need ḥalitza from the brothers."
But according to you,

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֲלִיצָה מִן הָאַחִין״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have taught "she does not need ḥalitza from the brothers"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the exchange in steps 12–13, with ריש לקיש now attacking.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that חליצה of a pregnant woman counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חליצה counted, the משנה should have taught the bigger point, that she needs no more חליצה from the brothers, instead of only the smaller point about כהונה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers that the wording matches the first part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees that she does not need חליצה from the brothers. The משנה said 'disqualified her' only to match its first part, which said 'did not disqualify her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, that is indeed so. But since the first part taught 'he did not disqualify her,' the last part also taught 'he disqualified her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's challenge. He explains why the משנה chose this wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן admits that, in his view, she really does not need more חליצה. The משנה did not say so because its first part spoke about being disqualified from כהונה, so the last part kept the same subject to make a clean contrast. The wording comes from the structure of the משנה, not from the law being smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (agreeing with the point)
Since it taught (wording chosen to match another part)
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רבי יוחנן holds the חליצה fully counted. The משנה's mention of כהונה is just there to match the wording of its first part.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, that is indeed so.
And since the first part taught "he did not disqualify her"
the last part also taught "he disqualified her."
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets, "also." The meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording parallelism (איידי): the משנה's choice of words matches its first part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions only the כהונה disqualification, so the חליצה must not have fully worked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חליצה fully worked. The משנה said 'disqualified her' only to contrast with 'did not disqualify her' in the first part.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the case of ייבום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the משנה's ruling that if he did ייבום with a pregnant יבמה and the baby is not viable, he may keep her. This fits his view that such ייבום counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: If the child is not viable, he may keep her. Granted, according to me, since I say that חליצה of a pregnant woman counts as חליצה and ביאה with a pregnant woman counts as ביאה, that is why it teaches 'he may keep her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now attacks ריש לקיש from another part of the משנה, about ייבום. He first shows how the משנה fits his own view, which sets up his question against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the baby is not viable, the man who did ייבום may keep her as his wife. For רבי יוחנן this is simple, because the ביאה counted as a real ייבום from the start. The unspoken challenge is that for ריש לקיש the ביאה did not count, so it is hard to see why he may simply keep her.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her (as his wife)
Marital relations, which is how ייבום is done
It is considered (literally, 'its name is')

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If the child is not viable — he may keep her.
Granted, according to me, since I say
the ḥalitza of a pregnant woman is considered ḥalitza,
and relations with a pregnant woman are considered relations,
that is why it teaches "he may keep her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, in the main version where רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש, this time from the ייבום clause of the משנה (step 4) instead of the חליצה clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that ייבום or חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets him keep her, which suggests the ביאה was a valid ייבום. This fits רבי יוחנן's view, and the question of how ריש לקיש explains it is set up for the next line.

steps.title: According to ריש לקיש, the משנה should have said 'do ייבום again'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes his challenge. If ייבום with a pregnant woman does not count, the משנה should have said he must do ייבום again and then keep her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to you, since you say that חליצה with a pregnant woman is not called חליצה, and ביאה with a pregnant woman is not called ביאה, the משנה should have said 'he must do ייבום again and then keep her'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן completes the challenge he began in step 16. He says the משנה's plain wording, 'he may keep her,' does not fit ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריש לקיש's view, the first ביאה did nothing, so the man has not yet done a real ייבום. The משנה should then have told him to do ייבום again before keeping her. Since it just says 'keep her,' it sounds like the first ביאה already counted.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you
A pregnant woman
It is not counted as a real ביאה (ייבום)
It should have said

phrases.english: But according to you,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרַתְּ חֲלִיצַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת — לֹא שְׁמָהּ חֲלִיצָה,
phrases.english: since you say that חליצה with a pregnant woman is not called חליצה,
and ביאה with a pregnant woman is not called ביאה,
the משנה should have said: 'He must do ביאה again and then keep her'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 16 by stating the problem for ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that ייבום with a pregnant woman does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first ביאה did nothing, the משנה should have required a new ביאה, not simply 'keep her.'

steps.title: 'Keep her' already means doing ייבום again
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that 'יקיים' really means he must do ייבום again and then keep her, because nothing else is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he may keep her' mean? It means he must do ביאה again and then keep her, because otherwise it is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge. He says the short word 'keep her' already includes the idea of doing ייבום again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no way to really 'keep' her as a wife without a valid ייבום. Since the first one did not count, 'keep her' must mean 'do it again and keep her.' The משנה did not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her (as his wife)
Because it is not enough (any other way)

phrases.english: What does 'he may keep her' mean?
He must do ביאה again and then keep her,
because otherwise it is not enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the short word includes the unstated step.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Keep her' means the first ביאה was enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Keep her' means do ייבום again and then keep her, since nothing less works.

steps.title: Second version: ריש לקיש uses 'keep her' against רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: In another version, ריש לקיש says the word 'יקיים' fits him, because it means 'do ייבום again.' For רבי יוחנן, the משנה should have said 'if he wants he divorces her, if he wants he keeps her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן from the משנה: 'If the baby is not viable, he may keep her.' It works for me, since I say חליצה and ביאה with a pregnant woman do not count. That is why it says 'keep her,' meaning 'do ביאה again and keep her,' since otherwise it is not enough. But according to you, it should have said 'if he wants, he divorces her; if he wants, he keeps her'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the argument. This time ריש לקיש uses the same word 'keep her' to challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says 'keep her' is a command-like word that fits his view: he has to do ייבום again. But if the first ביאה already counted, as רבי יוחנן holds, she is fully his wife. Then he could choose freely, so the משנה should have offered both choices: divorce or keep.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version)
It works well for me
If he wants, he divorces her
Without this

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה and the same word 'יקיים' as step 16. The two versions just switch who uses it to attack whom.

phrases.english: Some say:
ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן:
'If the baby is not viable, he may keep her.'
It works well for me, since I say
that חליצה with a pregnant woman is not called חליצה,
and ביאה with a pregnant woman is not called ביאה.
That is why it teaches 'he may keep her,'
meaning 'he must do ביאה again and then keep her,'
because without this it is not enough.
But according to you,
it should have said: 'If he wants, he divorces her; if he wants, he keeps her'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of steps 16-18, reversing who challenges whom.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that ייבום with a pregnant woman counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is already his full wife, the משנה should have offered a free choice (divorce or keep), not just 'keep her.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the wording just matches the first part
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees he really has a free choice. The משנה said 'keep her' only to contrast with its first part, which said 'divorce her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But since the first part taught 'he must divorce her,' the last part taught 'he may keep her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש. He admits the full law is a free choice, but explains why the משנה wrote it the way it did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first part (viable baby) said 'divorce her.' To make a neat contrast, the last part (non-viable baby) said simply 'keep her.' This is the same kind of answer as step 15: the wording follows the first part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is true
Since / because of
The first part
The last part

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, each side explains 'keep her' to fit his view: ריש לקיש says it means 'do ייבום again,' רבי יוחנן says it is just a contrast to 'divorce her.'

phrases.english: Yes, that is true,
but since the first part taught 'he must divorce her,'
the last part also taught 'he may keep her.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Style of the משנה: the wording is chosen to match the first part.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Keep her' means he has no choice but to keep her, so the first ביאה did not fully count.
steps.terutzMaskana: He really may choose; the משנה just wrote 'keep her' as a contrast to 'divorce her.'

steps.title: A ברייתא about the צרה when the יבמה turns out pregnant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if a man did ייבום and she turned out to be pregnant, her צרה may not marry, 'in case the baby is viable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If someone does ייבום with his יבמה and she turns out to be pregnant, her צרה may not marry, in case the baby is viable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next steps first fix its wording before the challenge is fully explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling says the צרה (the other wife of the dead brother) is not free to marry anyone. That ruling will become the basis for a challenge. But the reason the ברייתא gives seems backwards, so the גמרא deals with that first.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a teaching of the תנאים)
One who does ייבום with his יבמה
Her rival wife (the dead brother's other wife)
A viable baby

phrases.english: They challenged:
One who does ייבום with his יבמה
and she turns out to be pregnant,
her צרה may not marry,
in case the baby is viable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַכּוֹנֵס אֶת יְבִמְתּוֹ וְנִמְצֵאת מְעוּבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה and opens a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that ייבום with a pregnant woman counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא keeps the צרה from marrying. The full attack is explained after the wording is fixed.

steps.title: The ברייתא's reason seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the baby is viable, there is no ייבום at all, so the צרה would be free. The worry should be the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! When the baby is viable, her צרה is freed!
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא, the גמרא points out that its reason does not make sense as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dead brother left a viable child, there is no ייבום obligation, so the צרה is free to marry anyone. So a viable baby cannot be the reason to stop her. The worry must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
She is freed (from ייבום)

phrases.english: On the contrary,
when the baby is viable,
her צרה is freed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, כִּי הָוֵי הַוָּלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason given in the ברייתא quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא's reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A viable child frees the צרה, so it cannot be the reason she is forbidden to marry.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: 'in case the baby is NOT viable'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא to read: the צרה may not marry in case the baby is not viable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: in case the baby is not viable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording so its reason makes sense. This sets up the real challenge to רבי יוחנן, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is not viable, there was a ייבום obligation all along, so the צרה would still be tied to it. Now the ברייתא's worry makes sense. With this corrected reading, the גמרא can now build its challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read the text this way)

phrases.english: Rather, say:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא יְהֵא הַוָּלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא.
phrases.english: in case the baby is not viable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: שֶׁמָּא לֹא יְהֵא הַוָּלָד בֶּן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry is that the baby might be viable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is that the baby might not be viable, so the צרה may still be tied to ייבום.

steps.title: Why the Corrected ברייתא Challenges רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: If ביאה with a pregnant woman counted, the צרה should be freed by her fellow wife's ביאה. So why does the ברייתא forbid her to marry?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that ביאה with a pregnant woman counts as a real ביאה, why may her צרה not marry? She should be released through the ביאה done with her fellow wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the corrected ברייתא from Step 23 is a problem for the way רבי יוחנן's view was presented earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the brother does ייבום with one wife, all the other wives (the צרות) are freed. If ביאה with a pregnant woman counted, the צרה would already be free, whether the baby lives or not. Since the ברייתא forbids her to marry, it seems that this ביאה does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you think that)
Intercourse (ייבום) with a pregnant woman
It is called (counts as) a real ביאה
Her rival wife (the other wife of the dead brother)
Let her be released (from the ייבום bond)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that intercourse with a pregnant woman counts as intercourse,
why may her rival wife not marry?
Let her be released by the intercourse of her fellow wife!
phrases.notes: One wife's ייבום frees all the other wives, so the צרה should already be free.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בִּיאַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה, אַמַּאי לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא צָרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the consequence of the corrected ברייתא and aims it at רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The presented view of רבי יוחנן that ביאה with a pregnant woman counts as ביאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ביאה counted, it would free the צרה no matter what happens to the baby. The ברייתא forbids the צרה to marry, so the ביאה must not count.

steps.title: אביי: Everyone Agrees About ביאה, and the Argument Is About חליצה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that all agree ביאה with a pregnant woman frees no one. The מחלוקת is only about חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Regarding ביאה, everyone agrees that it does not release her. Where they disagree is regarding חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יוחנן by moving the argument. Nobody says ביאה with a pregnant woman counts, so the ברייתא is not a problem for anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 24 worked only if רבי יוחנן held that this ביאה counts. אביי says he never held that. The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש was really about חליצה done with a pregnant woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (all opinions)
They do not disagree
It releases her (from the ייבום bond)
The ceremony that releases a יבמה without ייבום

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבִיאָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא פָּטְרָה,
phrases.english: Regarding intercourse, everyone agrees that it does not release her;
where they disagree is regarding חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּבִיאָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא פָּטְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24 by moving the מחלוקת from ביאה to חליצה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the subject of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן held that ביאה with a pregnant woman counts, so the ברייתא refuted him.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree that ביאה with a pregnant woman does not count. The argument is only about חליצה, so the ברייתא fits everyone.

steps.title: אביי Spells Out Each Side's View
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: חליצה with a pregnant woman counts, but ביאה does not. ריש לקיש: neither one counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds: חליצה with a pregnant woman counts as חליצה, but ביאה with a pregnant woman does not count as ביאה. ריש לקיש holds: ביאה with a pregnant woman does not count as ביאה, and חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count as חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his answer and lays out exactly what each אמורא holds under his new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן now splits the two acts: חליצה works, but ביאה does not. ריש לקיש treats them the same, and neither works. This split in רבי יוחנן's view is what רבא will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
חליצה done with a pregnant woman
It is not called (does not count as)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי: רבי יוחנן says חליצה with a pregnant woman works but ביאה does not. ריש לקיש says neither works.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan holds:
חליצה with a pregnant woman counts as חליצה,
but intercourse with a pregnant woman does not count as intercourse.
Reish Lakish holds:
intercourse with a pregnant woman does not count as intercourse,
and חליצה with a pregnant woman does not count as חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: חֲלִיצַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת שְׁמָהּ חֲלִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the details of אביי's answer from Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: חליצה with a pregnant woman is valid, but ביאה is not. ריש לקיש: neither is valid.

steps.title: רבא: ביאה and חליצה Must Go Together
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues 'whichever way you look at it': if ביאה with a pregnant woman counts, so does חליצה, and if it does not, then חליצה does not either. He then begins to bring a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Whichever way you look at it, if ביאה with a pregnant woman counts as ביאה, then חליצה with a pregnant woman counts as חליצה. And if ביאה with a pregnant woman does not count as ביאה, then חליצה with a pregnant woman also does not count as חליצה. For we hold that...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's version of רבי יוחנן. He says you cannot split ביאה and חליצה the way אביי did. The step ends as רבא starts to bring his source, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'מה נפשך' argument checks both possibilities and shows that each one leads to the same problem. Here, both choices make ביאה and חליצה equal, so רבי יוחנן's split (חליצה works but ביאה does not) makes no sense. The words 'דהא קיימא לן' introduce a known rule that will explain why the two are tied together.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (both options lead to the same result)
Also
For we hold as an established rule

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's sentence is not finished here. 'דהא קיימא לן' opens the rule he relies on, and that rule continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: Whichever way you look at it:
if intercourse with a pregnant woman counts as intercourse,
then חליצה with a pregnant woman counts as חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בִּיאַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת לֹא שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה —
phrases.english: And if intercourse with a pregnant woman does not count as intercourse,

phrases.aramaic: חֲלִיצַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת נָמֵי לֹא שְׁמָהּ חֲלִיצָה.
phrases.english: then חליצה with a pregnant woman also does not count as חליצה.
For we hold as an established rule,
phrases.notes: The rule itself comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the split in רבי יוחנן's view that אביי described in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי יוחנן treats חליצה with a pregnant woman as valid but ביאה as invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'מה נפשך' argument: under either possibility, ביאה and חליצה must have the same status, so they cannot be split. A supporting rule ('דהא קיימא לן') is about to be brought.
